evidence: refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5-14 returns the raw fetch Response when sync is enabled. zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:204-217 wraps an axios call and then reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error. A fetch Response has no .data, so this throws a TypeError. The surrounding catch only logs it, so the token is never refreshed in sync mode.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17-93 never checks req.method, so any verb that passes the secret check creates or updates credentials. Other API routes guard on req.method (e.g. apps/web/pages/api/availability/calendar.ts, auth/reset-password.ts) or use defaultHandler({POST: ...}) (recorded-daily-video.ts:210). The secret check still applies, so impact is low; this is hardening.

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 POSTs to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only calcomUserId and appSlug, and no shared secret or auth header. The parent app therefore cannot authenticate Cal.com, and anyone who can reach that endpoint can request live tokens for any userId. The content-type part is wrong: fetch with a URLSearchParams body sets application/x-www-form-urlencoded automatically. The SSRF framing is overstated because the URL comes from admin-controlled env.

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11: z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() both evaluate at runtime to the literal key "[object Object]" (confirmed with node). The second key overwrites the first, so the schema is {access_token, "[object Object]"?: unknown}. Because z.object strips unknown keys by default, expiry fields such as expires_in and expiry_date are dropped from .data in sync mode. The reviewer's 'build time' wording is slightly off (it happens at runtime), but the conclusion is correct.

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 fills a missing refresh_token with the literal string 'refresh_token'. zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:116-120 then writes key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token to the DB. office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 spreads tokenResponse.data over the stored credentials, which also overwrites the real refresh_token. Salesforce (CalendarService.ts:98) explicitly restores it, which shows the overwrite is a real hazard.

googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-96: the non-sync callback returns a gaxios res, and the code reads res?.data.access_token. In sync mode the return is a fetch Response, so res.data is undefined and token.access_token throws. The catch at ~104 returns myGoogleAuth without new tokens. Separately, line 97 stores the whole SafeParse result object ({success, data}) as the credential key, which is another bug.

zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:69 has refreshAccessToken(credentialId, ...), and lines 85-94 pass credentialId as refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter, which is userId (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3). The sync endpoint gets a credential PK as calcomUserId. Every other caller passes credential.userId. Team credentials (userId null) would also wrongly take the sync path.

salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 calls prisma.credential.update(...), but the file's imports (lines 1-20) have no prisma import; grep finds 'prisma' only on line 96. This fails type-checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.

app-credential.ts:31 uses .parse(req.body) in a plain Next handler with no defaultHandler/defaultResponder wrapper, so a ZodError becomes an unhandled 500. Lines 56-58 (symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse) also throw 500s on bad input. Using safeParse and returning 400 is better webhook behavior. It is not a security or correctness bug.

hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-200: in sync mode the result is a fetch Response cast to HubspotToken. expiresIn is undefined, so expiryDate becomes NaN. The Response object is then written as the credential key, and setAccessToken(undefined) is called. Refresh breaks in sync mode.

app-credential.ts:24-29: Node's IncomingMessage joins duplicate custom headers into one comma-separated string; only set-cookie becomes an array. Even if the value were an array, the strict !== comparison would fail and return 403, so the check fails closed and cannot be bypassed. APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED (constants.ts:103-104) requires CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET to be truthy, so a missing header cannot match an empty secret. A timing-safe compare would be a separate, unclaimed improvement.

salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 checks response.statusText !== 'OK'. The reason phrase is optional (HTTP/2 has none, and fetch then returns an empty statusText), so successful responses could be treated as errors. response.ok or response.status is the reliable check. In practice, Node's undici over HTTP/1.1 currently returns 'OK'.

salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:89-98: in sync mode parseRefreshTokenResponse uses minimumTokenResponseSchema, which strips everything except access_token (see issue 3). The DB key then becomes {access_token, refresh_token}, losing instance_url, id, issued_at and the other fields. Later calls read credentialKey.instance_url (line ~104), which would be undefined.

constants.ts:103-104: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = SECRET && KEY, typed string | undefined, and it actually holds the encryption key value. Every use site (app-credential.ts:19, refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5, parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15) is a truthy check, so nothing breaks at runtime. Wrapping it in !!(...) is a naming/type clarity improvement.

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-20 returns a fetch Response in sync mode, but refreshFunction() returns an axios response (zohocrm, zoho-bigin), a gaxios res (google) or a HubspotToken (hubspot). Fetch-based callers (zoom, office365, webex, lark) are compatible; the others break, as in issues 0, 5 and 9. Root-cause fix: normalize the return type (e.g. return parsed JSON in both branches) or adapt each caller.
